# BMS / DJMax Keysound Slicer UX audit

## Scope and evidence note
This is an evidence-led audit of pages retrievable in this run. Community guides often conflate Woslicer II and III, so version-specific behavior is labelled where the guide is explicit. Sayaslicer’s issues index exposed no list in the retrieved page; the only concrete issue I could verify directly was the documented large-file issue #5, so I do **not** invent a ‘top 10 GitHub issues’ list. ([Sayaslicer issues](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer/issues), [issue #5](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer/issues/5))

## 1. Comparison table

| Tool | Workflow | Top 3 pain points / limits | Max slices / snap | Export method |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Sayaslicer | Load/drag audio; place or import markers; adjust offset/snap and optional zero-cross, fade and silent-tail processing; save project; copy markers to BMSE or iBMSC, export WAVs and/or keysound list. ([README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#readme)) | Zero-crossing moves markers and can make iBMSC data troublesome; the README recommends BMSE fallback when pasted data causes missing keysounds/gamemode changes; partial BPM support is explicitly “a bit hackish.” ([README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#readme)) | Snap 1/1–1/192; iBMSC path can carry over-192nd markers; no hard slice-count cap stated. ([README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#readme)) | WAV/key­sound export; BMSE clipboard, iBMSC clipboard, keysound-list export; optional base-62 BMSE clipboard. ([README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#readme)) |
| Woslicer II | Load WAV, set BPM/offset/grid, mark cuts, preview, batch export numbered WAVs; paste placement data into BMSE. ([DTM Tech BMS guide](http://dtmtechbms.web.fc2.com/0008/0008.html)) | Offset alignment is manual; tails/endpoints need adjustment; output is numbered files in the source folder, creating a file-management step. ([DTM Tech BMS guide](http://dtmtechbms.web.fc2.com/0008/0008.html)) | Guide says newer versions load much longer WAVs, but gives no hard slice maximum; default grid is described as sixteenth and can be changed. ([DTM Tech BMS guide](http://dtmtechbms.web.fc2.com/0008/0008.html)) | Sequential WAV files plus clipboard placement data. ([DTM Tech BMS guide](http://dtmtechbms.web.fc2.com/0008/0008.html)) |
| Woslicer III | Create/save BMS; drag WAV; choose start/BPM; click bar lines; output WAV and `.wos`; define files in BMSE; reload `.wos`, clipboard-output sequence, paste into BMSE. ([Purureko](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/), [BMS guide](https://spirea3cross.wixsite.com/bmstukuru2020/how-to-make3)) | Three-tool clipboard ceremony; Explorer ordering and first-file selection affect definition numbering; a guide says disabled batch output can be fixed by making the filename appear in the lower-left field; tails may need cleanup. ([Purureko](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/)) | No hard max stated. Practical BMS guidance says avoid segments ≥60 seconds and recommends about 50 seconds; four-digit filenames may occur. ([BMS guide](https://spirea3cross.wixsite.com/bmstukuru2020/how-to-make3)) | WAV output, reusable `.wos` cut-position project, clipboard sequence output. ([Purureko](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/)) |
| BMHelper | Arrange MIDI/audio to reduce unique sounds; render; copy cut positions; slice externally; insert generated definitions/sequence into BMSE/iBMSC. ([BMHelper](https://excln.github.io/bmhelper.html), [BMHelper wiki](https://wiki.mid2bms.net/%E4%BB%96%E3%83%84%E3%83%BC%E3%83%AB/Be-Music%20Helper)) | Not a complete slicer; still requires editor and clipboard handoffs; MIDI/automation-heavy parts can require manual rough chopping. ([BMHelper](https://excln.github.io/bmhelper.html), [Purureko](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/)) | No BMHelper-specific numeric cap found; downstream BMS identifiers are commonly base-36, 1296 codes with `00` conventionally reserved, i.e. 1295 practical slots. ([NamuWiki](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%ED%82%A4%EC%9D%8C), [BMS command reference](https://hitkey.nekokan.dyndns.info/cmds.htm)) | Clipboard cut positions and editor insertion; audio rendered/sliced by another tool. ([BMHelper](https://excln.github.io/bmhelper.html)) |
| Mid2BMS | Export MIDI from DAW; use named tracks/rendered WAV and Mid2BMS to create renamed WAVs and BMS text; combine generated data in BMSE. ([Mid2BMS](https://mid2bms.net/), [tutorial](https://trap.jp/post/777/)) | Track names and paths must be organized; red mode requires “same sound once,” then repeated notes must be restored manually in BMSE/iBMSC; generated text/WAV files can land beside source files. ([tutorial](https://trap.jp/post/777/)) | No numeric Mid2BMS ceiling found; output remains constrained by target BMS/editor identifier capacity. ([Mid2BMS](https://mid2bms.net/), [BMS command reference](https://hitkey.nekokan.dyndns.info/cmds.htm)) | Generated WAVs plus BMS text/renamer-array files. ([Mid2BMS](https://mid2bms.net/)) |
| PTSEQUENCER / DJMAX-era constraints | Build a game-specific sample table and map note events to it; reduce or merge samples when the target cap is reached. ([NamuWiki](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%ED%82%A4%EC%9D음)) | Game-specific caps do not transfer from BMS; excessive loaded files are a practical concern; older key-sound playback can cut/restart sounds on a lane. ([NamuWiki](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%ED%82%A4%EC%9음)) | NamuWiki reports historical values of 255 for older EZ2AC, 2047 for later EZ2AC, and 1023 for PTSEQUENCER/DJMAX-era tooling; verify the exact target build. ([NamuWiki](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%ED%82%키음)) | Game-specific asset table, not BMSE clipboard. ([NamuWiki](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%ED%82%A키음)) |
| dtinth/sound-slicer | Put source WAV and `.txt` cut descriptions in a project folder; generate sliced WAVs and BMS clipboard; rhythmic mode slices every event, melodic mode groups by note/length/velocity and reuses fewer slices. ([repo](https://github.com/dtinth/sound-slicer)) | Rhythmic mode can create 1000 slices for 1000 notes and can leave gaps; melodic mode requires re-rendering a reorganized MIDI; both modes do not support BPM changes. ([repo](https://github.com/dtinth/sound-slicer)) | No hard cap; repo is old (2011 history) and is WAV/script-oriented. ([repo](https://github.com/dtinth/sound-slicer)) | Numbered WAVs in a `wav` subfolder and BMS clipboard file. ([repo](https://github.com/dtinth/sound-slicer)) |

## 2. Problem inventory

### Timeline / timing

| Severity | Problem | Evidence and implication |
|---|---|---|
| P0 | Destructive slicing separates a visual cut from the final chart object. Users must render WAVs, define them, then paste timing data into an editor. | sound-slicer explicitly emits parts plus a clipboard file; Woslicer guides require WAV output, definition, then clipboard paste. ([sound-slicer](https://github.com/dtinth/sound-slicer), [Purureko](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/)) |
| P0 | Marker correction can alter musical timing. Sayaslicer’s zero-crossing moves markers and can invalidate fine iBMSC clipboard placement. | ([Sayaslicer README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#readme)) |
| P1 | BPM/offset is not a single reliable source of truth. Woslicer requires start/offset adjustment; Sayaslicer calls partial BPM support hackish; sound-slicer does not support BPM changes. | ([Woslicer guide](http://dtmtechbms.web.fc2.com/0008/0008.html), [Sayaslicer README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#readme), [sound-slicer](https://github.com/dtinth/sound-slicer)) |
| P1 | Coarse quantization can change intended timing. Modern BMS guidance warns that a 192 default can snap finer timing. | ([BMS checklist](https://wcko87.github.io/bms-checklist/)) |
| P1 | Users cannot safely judge whether a long tail belongs to the current note. Community guides explicitly warn to adjust endpoints/tails and keep key sounds below about a minute. | ([DTM guide](http://dtmtechbms.web.fc2.com/0008/0008.html), [BMS guide](https://spirea3cross.wixsite.com/bmstukuru2020/how-to-make3)) |

### Interface / workflow

| Severity | Problem | Evidence and implication |
|---|---|---|
| P0 | The export ceremony is multi-application and stateful: BMHelper → slicer → file explorer → BMSE/iBMSC → clipboard. | ([Purureko](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/), [BMHelper](https://excln.github.io/bmhelper.html)) |
| P0 | File order is semantically meaningful. Selecting a middle WAV can shift definition numbering and requires retrying. | ([Purureko](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/)) |
| P1 | Batch output can fail for a non-obvious UI reason: the Woslicer guide says the filename must appear in a lower-left field before “export all” is enabled; clicking the black area may reveal it. | ([Purureko](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/)) |
| P1 | Keyboard-heavy operation and tool-specific clipboard formats raise mode errors. Sayaslicer documents extensive keyboard commands and separate BMSE/iBMSC clipboard routes; Woslicer guides require remembering menu direction. | ([Sayaslicer README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#readme), [Purureko](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/)) |
| P2 | Legacy tooling and compatibility are risks: sound-slicer’s repository history is from 2011, while current BMS resource guidance describes LR2 as over ten years old and buggy. | ([sound-slicer](https://github.com/dtinth/sound-slicer), [BMS resources](https://bms-community.github.io/resources/)) |

### Settings / compatibility

| Severity | Problem | Evidence and implication |
|---|---|---|
| P0 | Identifier overflow/interoperability. Base-36 provides 1296 two-character codes, with `00` conventionally empty; base-62 expands capacity but is not a universal BMS guarantee. | ([BMS command reference](https://hitkey.nekokan.dyndns.info/cmds.htm), [Sayaslicer README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#readme), [NamuWiki](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%ED%82%A4%E9%음)) |
| P1 | No documented unified per-slice policy for zero-cross, fade, tail trimming and normalization. Existing tools expose some global/export settings; Sayaslicer’s zero-cross behavior is particularly coupled to marker positions. | ([Sayaslicer README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#readme)) |
| P1 | Format constraints leak into authoring: sound-slicer reads WAV; FL Studio’s Fruity Slicer says MP3 cannot contain slice markers, only WAV, and recommends zero-cross/declick for clicks. | ([Fruity Slicer manual](https://www.image-line.com/fl-studio-learning/fl-studio-online-manual/html/plugins/Fruity%20Slicer.htm)) |
| P2 | Hard limits are often undocumented or target-specific. Guides state no Woslicer or Mid2BMS slice maximum; PTSEQUENCER figures are historical and should not be treated as current SDK guarantees. | ([Woslicer guide](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/), [Mid2BMS](https://mid2bms.net/), [NamuWiki](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%ED%82%A4%EC%9음)) |

### Backend / audio

| Severity | Problem | Evidence and implication |
|---|---|---|
| P0 | Audio is duplicated into hundreds/thousands of files before the chart is validated. sound-slicer’s documented project layout stores every numbered WAV in a subfolder; rhythmic mode can produce one per event. | ([sound-slicer](https://github.com/dtinth/sound-slicer)) |
| P1 | Large source files can make slicers unusable. Sayaslicer issue #5 documents >2 GB files causing lag/unusability due to an OpenAL signed-int buffer-size overflow; the issue was later fixed. | ([issue #5](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer/issues/5)) |
| P1 | Clicks and reverb-tail cutoffs require destructive correction or export-time settings. Woslicer community material warns about tails; Sayaslicer provides zero-cross, fade and silent-tail removal, but zero-cross changes positions. | ([DTM guide](http://dtmtechbms.web.fc2.com/0008/0008.html), [Sayaslicer README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#readme)) |
| P1 | Reuse is manual/heuristic rather than a first-class object. sound-slicer’s melodic mode can reduce 500 repeated bass notes to 10 slices, but requires a reorganized MIDI/render pass. | ([sound-slicer](https://github.com/dtinth/sound-slicer)) |
| P2 | Export assets and source edits can diverge. Mid2BMS tutorials warn about generated files/paths and a renamer-array workaround, illustrating fragile build artifacts. | ([Mid2BMS tutorial](https://trap.jp/post/777/)) |

## 3. What Sayaslicer did right vs Woslicer (keep these)

### Keep from Sayaslicer
1. Preserve the proven BMSE clipboard path while adding iBMSC export for finer-than-192nd markers. ([README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#readme))
2. Make base-62 opt-in rather than silently emitting incompatible data. ([README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#readme))
3. Treat zero-cross as an explicit trade-off: it can reduce clicks but moves markers, and the UI warns about downstream impact. ([README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#readme))
4. Keep projects, marker copy/paste, undo/redo, MIDI import and Mid2BMS array import in the same tool. ([README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#readme))
5. Provide practical keyboard acceleration: marker insertion, preview-and-advance, jump by marker, snap changes, export and project save. ([README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#readme))

### Keep from Woslicer
1. Fast waveform marking with a visible BPM/grid and preview-to-next-marker. ([DTM guide](http://dtmtechbms.web.fc2.com/0008/0008.html))
2. Reusable cut-position project (`.wos`) so a cut pattern can be applied again. ([Purureko](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/))
3. Simple batch export for compatibility with editors that require discrete WAV assets. ([Purureko](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/))
4. Clipboard import/export that preserves a practical bridge to BMSE. ([Purureko](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/))

## 4. Top 10 recommendations for DJMax Studio slicer

1. **P0 — Make virtual slices the canonical object.** Store `{sourceFile,startMs,endMs}` plus stable slice ID, gain/fade/zero-cross metadata; render WAV/OGG only on finalize. This directly removes the WAV-and-clipboard ceremony documented by sound-slicer and Woslicer. ([sound-slicer](https://github.com/dtinth/sound-slicer), [Purureko](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/))
2. **P0 — Add a dual timeline.** Put waveform/time ruler below and Studio chart preview/notes above, with one shared playhead and click-to-audition. Existing tools expose waveform cuts but not a unified chart preview; their workflows instead export then paste into BMSE. ([Sayaslicer README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#readme), [Purureko](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/))
3. **P0 — Make timing provenance visible.** Show ms, bar/beat, BPM segment and quantized target together; allow Grid/Beat/Off auto-advance and an explicit “resnap” command. Sayaslicer exposes offset/arbitrary snap and a resnap-all feature, while partial BPM is a known weak spot. ([Sayaslicer README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#readme))
4. **P0 — Separate musical position from audio cleanup.** Zero-cross should adjust an audio boundary/fade independently of the note’s authored timestamp, with before/after preview and a warning when it changes the chart position. The current coupling is a documented Sayaslicer problem. ([README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#readme))
5. **P1 — Provide per-slice overrides.** Expose zero-cross on/off, fade-in/out, tail trim, gain/normalize and audition on each slice, with global defaults. This targets documented click/tail problems while avoiding global destructive edits. ([Sayaslicer README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#readme), [DTM guide](http://dtmtechbms.web.fc2.com/0008/0008.html), [Fruity Slicer manual](https://www.image-line.com/fl-studio-learning/fl-studio-online-manual/html/plugins/Fruity%20Slicer.htm))
6. **P1 — Make reuse and dedup first-class.** Let many notes reference one slice, but permit occurrence-level gain/fade; offer a melodic-style “suggest reuse” pass rather than forcing a re-rendered MIDI. sound-slicer demonstrates the value of reuse, but its implementation requires a separate render workflow. ([sound-slicer](https://github.com/dtinth/sound-slicer))
7. **P1 — Build target-aware preflight.** Select BMS / RESPECT / TECHNIKA; show identifier budget, format, maximum-duration warnings, stereo/sample-rate policy and compatibility risks before export. Base-36/base-62 and game-specific counts differ materially. ([BMS command reference](https://hitkey.nekokan.dyndns.info/cmds.htm), [NamuWiki](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%ED%82%A4%EC%9음))
8. **P1 — One-click “Import to Studio” and round-trip.** Accept BMSE/iBMSC clipboard, MIDI, Mid2BMS arrays and `.wos`; export back without losing slice IDs or chart positions. Existing integrations are clipboard/file based and can mis-number when Explorer order changes. ([Sayaslicer README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#readme), [Purureko](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/))
9. **P1 — Make large audio streamable.** Use waveform tiles/proxies and bounded decoding, avoiding whole-file buffers; add a test for >2 GB sources because Sayaslicer’s issue #5 identified an OpenAL integer overflow. ([issue #5](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer/issues/5))
10. **P2 — Add an explicit export/build manifest and QA.** Deterministically map stable IDs to filenames, preserve source/marker metadata, preview the finalized chart, and validate clicks, missing assets, duplicate IDs, over-duration slices and encoding. Existing guidance requires packaging/format and clipping checks, while older workflows scatter artifacts across folders. ([BMS checklist](https://wcko87.github.io/bms-checklist/), [Mid2BMS tutorial](https://trap.jp/post/777/), [sound-slicer](https://github.com/dtinth/sound-slicer))

## Proposed feature validation
The proposed dual timeline and “Import to Studio” are strongly supported by the observed gap: Woslicer and sound-slicer expose waveform cutting plus an exported clipboard/file, while Sayaslicer exposes marker interchange but still warns that zero-cross can break fine clipboard placement. ([sound-slicer](https://github.com/dtinth/sound-slicer), [Woslicer guide](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/), [Sayaslicer README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#readme))

A BMS/RESPECT/TECHNIKA mode switcher is also justified, but the modes must be capability profiles rather than cosmetic labels: BMS uses editor/player-dependent object alphabets; DJMAX-family historical limits and same-lane playback behavior differ; and the accessible sources do not establish a current official RESPECT or TECHNIKA authoring specification. ([BMS command reference](https://hitkey.nekokan.dyndns.info/cmds.htm), [NamuWiki](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%ED%82%A4%EC%9음))

## Evidence gaps
No usable issue/discussion list was exposed for Sayaslicer beyond issue #5; no verifiable YouTube comment corpus was accessible; and no authoritative current PTSEQUENCER/RESPECT/TECHNIKA authoring SDK specification was found. Historical/community claims are labelled as such rather than presented as current product guarantees.
